# macOS Power Usage Prometheus Exporter

![Go](https://img.shields.io/badge/Go-1.26+-00ADD8?style=flat&logo=go)
![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)

This program exports the power usage of your macOS device as Prometheus metrics.

## Features

- Exports CPU, GPU, ANE (Apple Neural Engine), and combined power usage
- Prometheus metrics with hostname label
- Automatic reader restart on failure
- Graceful shutdown handling
- Health check endpoint

## Prerequisites

- Go 1.26 or later
- macOS (required for `powermetrics` command)
- `sudo` permissions (required for `powermetrics`)

> **Note:** This program cannot run in a container. The `powermetrics` command is a macOS-specific tool that requires direct hardware access to CPU, GPU, and ANE power sensors. It must run directly on a Mac.

## Installation

### From Source

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/combust-labs/macos-power-consumption-exporter.git
cd macos-power-consumption-exporter

# Build
make build

# Or install dependencies and build
make install
make build
```

### Pre-built Binaries

Download the latest release from the [Releases](https://github.com/combust-labs/macos-power-consumption-exporter/releases) page.

### DMG Installer (Recommended for macOS)

For a native macOS installation experience, download the DMG installer:

1. Download the latest `.dmg` file from [Releases](https://github.com/combust-labs/macos-power-consumption-exporter/releases)
2. Double-click the DMG to mount it
3. Drag "MacOS Power Consumption Exporter" to the Applications folder
4. Run the launcher to start the exporter (see below)

#### Starting the Exporter (After DMG Install)

The application includes a **launcher script** for managing the exporter. Since the app requires elevated privileges to access `powermetrics`, use Terminal to run it:

```bash
# Navigate to the app bundle
cd "/Applications/MacOS Power Consumption Exporter.app/Contents/MacOS"

# Install and start the exporter (requires admin password)
sudo ./launcher install
```

The launcher will:
- Install a launch agent for auto-start on login
- Start the exporter immediately
- Create log files in `~/Library/Logs/com.combust.macos-power-consumption-exporter/`

#### Launcher Commands

The launcher script supports the following commands:

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `sudo ./launcher install` | Install launch agent and start exporter |
| `sudo ./launcher start` | Start the exporter |
| `sudo ./launcher stop` | Stop the exporter |
| `./launcher status` | Check if exporter is running |
| `./launcher open` | Open metrics page in browser |
| `sudo ./launcher uninstall` | Stop and remove launch agent |

### xbar Integration (Optional)

For a menu bar display of power metrics without a GUI app, you can use **xbar**:

#### Installation

```bash
# Install xbar via Homebrew
brew install xbar

# Or download from: https://xbarapp.com
```

#### Setup

```bash
# Create plugins directory
mkdir -p ~/Library/Application\ Support/xbar/plugins

# Copy the power metrics plugin
cp installer/bitbar/power-metrics-simple.sh ~/Library/Application\ Support/xbar/plugins/power-metrics.10s.sh

# Make executable
chmod +x ~/Library/Application\ Support/xbar/plugins/power-metrics.10s.sh
```

#### Restart xbar

1. Click the xbar icon in the menu bar
2. Select "Refresh" or restart xbar

#### Features

The plugin displays:
- **Menu bar icon**: ⚡ (or 🔥 for high power, 🔋 for low power)
- **Combined power** in the menu bar (e.g., "⚡ 2.5W")
- **Dropdown menu** with:
  - Combined, CPU, GPU, ANE power values
  - Links to open metrics/health in browser
  - Options to restart/stop exporter
  - Auto-refresh every 10 seconds

#### Customization

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `installer/xbar/power-metrics.sh` | Full version with colors and more features |
| `installer/xbar/power-metrics-simple.sh` | Simpler version (no bc required) |

To change refresh rate, rename the file (e.g., `power-metrics.30s.sh` for 30 seconds).

#### Accessing Metrics

Once running, access the metrics at:

| Endpoint | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| http://localhost:8080/metrics | Prometheus metrics |
| http://localhost:8080/health | Health check |

#### Building the DMG from Source

```bash
# Clone and build
git clone https://github.com/combust-labs/macos-power-consumption-exporter.git
cd macos-power-consumption-exporter

# Build unsigned DMG (for development/testing)
make dmg-unsigned

# The DMG will be created at: dist/MacOS Power Consumption Exporter.dmg
```

For a signed DMG (for distribution), see the [Signing & Distribution](#signing--distribution) section.

## Usage

### Basic Usage

```bash
sudo ./macos-power-consumption-exporter
```

The exporter will start on `http://localhost:8080` by default.

### Custom Address

```bash
sudo ./macos-power-consumption-exporter -addr :9090
```

### Command-line Options

| Flag | Default | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `-addr` | `:8080` | HTTP server address |
| `-log-level` | `info` | Log level (debug, info, warn, error) |

### Makefile Targets

```bash
make build    # Build the binary
make test     # Run tests with coverage
make run      # Build and run (requires sudo)
make clean    # Clean build artifacts
```

## Prometheus Configuration

Add a scrape configuration to your `prometheus.yml`:

```yaml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: 'macos-power-usage'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['localhost:8080']
```

## Exported Metrics

| Metric | Type | Description | Labels |
|--------|------|-------------|--------|
| `power_usage_reader_cpu_power` | Gauge | CPU power in milliwatts | hostname |
| `power_usage_reader_gpu_power` | Gauge | GPU power in milliwatts | hostname |
| `power_usage_ane_power` | Gauge | Apple Neural Engine power in milliwatts | hostname |
| `power_usage_combined_power` | Gauge | Combined power (CPU + GPU + ANE) in milliwatts | hostname |
| `power_usage_reader_restart_count` | Counter | Number of reader restarts | hostname |

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `/metrics` | Prometheus metrics endpoint |
| `/health` | Health check endpoint |

## Architecture

This program contains two main components:

1. **Power Usage Reader** - Reads power metrics from the operating system using `powermetrics` command
2. **Power Usage Exporter** - HTTP server that exposes metrics to Prometheus

### Data Flow

```
powermetrics → Parser → Prometheus Metrics → HTTP Server → Prometheus
```

## Testing

```bash
# Run unit tests
go test ./...

# Run tests with coverage
make test

# Run specific test
go test -v ./internal/power_usage_reader/...
```

## Troubleshooting

### Permission Denied

The `powermetrics` command requires sudo permissions. Make sure to run the exporter with sudo:

```bash
# Command line usage
sudo ./macos-power-consumption-exporter

# Or via launcher (after DMG install)
cd "/Applications/MacOS Power Consumption Exporter.app/Contents/MacOS"
sudo ./launcher install
```

### Port Already in Use

If port 8080 is already in use, specify a different port:

```bash
sudo ./macos-power-consumption-exporter -addr :8081
```

### No Metrics Showing

Ensure `powermetrics` is available on your system:

```bash
sudo powermetrics --help
```

### Can I Run This in a Container?

**No.** This program cannot run in Docker, Kubernetes, or any container environment because:

- `powermetrics` is a macOS-specific command that requires direct hardware access
- It accesses CPU, GPU, and ANE power sensors that are not available in containers
- The program must run directly on a Mac with sudo privileges

## Uninstallation

### Via DMG Installer

If you installed via DMG:

1. Open Finder → Applications
2. Drag "MacOS Power Consumption Exporter" to Trash
3. Run the uninstall script (optional but recommended):

```bash
# Download and run uninstall script
curl -L -o uninstall.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/combust-labs/macos-power-consumption-exporter/main/installer/scripts/uninstall.sh
chmod +x uninstall.sh
./uninstall.sh
```

### Via Command Line

If you installed the binary manually:

```bash
# Stop the exporter if running
sudo pkill macos-power-consumption-exporter

# Remove the binary
sudo rm -f /usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption-exporter
```

### What Gets Removed

The uninstall script removes:
- Application bundle from `/Applications` or `~/Applications`
- Launch agent (`~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.combust.macos-power-consumption-exporter.plist`)
- Log files (`~/Library/Logs/com.combust.macos-power-consumption-exporter/`)
- Cache files (`~/Library/Caches/com.combust.macos-power-consumption-exporter/`)
- Preference files

## Signing & Distribution

For distribution outside the Mac App Store, you can sign and notarize the app:

### Prerequisites

- Apple Developer ID certificate
- App-specific password for notarization

### Build Signed DMG

```bash
# Set your certificate name
export CERTIFICATE="Developer ID Application: Your Name"

# Build signed DMG
make dmg
```

### Full Distribution Build

```bash
# Set all required environment variables
export CERTIFICATE="Developer ID Application: Your Name"
export APPLE_ID="your@email.com"
export APP_PASSWORD="app-specific-password"
export TEAM_ID="YOUR_TEAM_ID"

# Build, sign, notarize, and package
make dist
```

### Notes

- Unsigned DMGs will trigger Gatekeeper warnings
- Notarization is required for distribution outside the Mac App Store
- After notarization, users can run the app without disabling Gatekeeper

## License

MIT License - see [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please open an issue or submit a pull request.

#!/bin/bash
#
# macOS Power Consumption Exporter - Application Launcher
# This script is the entry point for the .app bundle
#

set -e

# Configuration
APP_NAME="MacOS Power Consumption Exporter"
BUNDLE_ID="com.combust.macos-power-consumption-exporter"
HELPER_LABEL="com.combust.macos-power-consumption-exporter"
EXPORTER_PORT="${EXPORTER_PORT:-8080}"
LOG_DIR="$HOME/Library/Logs/com.combust.macos-power-consumption-exporter"
PID_FILE="$HOME/.macos-power-consumption-exporter.pid"

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

log_info() {
    echo -e "${GREEN}[INFO]${NC} $1"
}

log_warn() {
    echo -e "${YELLOW}[WARN]${NC} $1"
}

log_error() {
    echo -e "${RED}[ERROR]${NC} $1"
}

# Get the directory where this script is located
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
BINARY_PATH="$SCRIPT_DIR/../MacOS/macos-power-consumption-exporter"

# Create log directory
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"

# Check if powermetrics is available
check_powermetrics() {
    if ! command -v powermetrics &> /dev/null; then
        log_error "powermetrics command not found. This application requires macOS."
        osascript -e 'display dialog "powermetrics not found. This application requires macOS." with title "Error" buttons {"OK"} with icon stop'
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Check if running with sudo privileges
check_sudo() {
    if [ "$EUID" -ne 0 ]; then
        log_warn "Not running with sudo privileges"
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# Install launch agent for current user
install_launch_agent() {
    local plist_dir="$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents"
    local plist_path="$plist_dir/${HELPER_LABEL}.plist"

    mkdir -p "$plist_dir"

    # Create launch agent plist
    cat > "$plist_path" << EOF
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>Label</key>
    <string>${HELPER_LABEL}</string>
    <key>ProgramArguments</key>
    <array>
        <string>${BINARY_PATH}</string>
        <string>-addr</string>
        <string>:${EXPORTER_PORT}</string>
    </array>
    <key>RunAtLoad</key>
    <true/>
    <key>KeepAlive</key>
    <true/>
    <key>StandardOutPath</key>
    <string>${LOG_DIR}/exporter.log</string>
    <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
    <string>${LOG_DIR}/exporter.error.log</string>
    <key>ProcessType</key>
    <string>Interactive</string>
</dict>
</plist>
EOF

    log_info "Launch agent installed at $plist_path"
}

# Uninstall launch agent
uninstall_launch_agent() {
    local plist_path="$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/${HELPER_LABEL}.plist"

    if [ -f "$plist_path" ]; then
        launchctl unload "$plist_path" 2>/dev/null || true
        rm -f "$plist_path"
        log_info "Launch agent uninstalled"
    fi
}

# Start the exporter
start_exporter() {
    # Check if already running
    if [ -f "$PID_FILE" ]; then
        local old_pid=$(cat "$PID_FILE")
        if kill -0 "$old_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
            log_info "Exporter is already running (PID: $old_pid)"
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Request sudo if needed
    if ! check_sudo; then
        log_warn "Starting without sudo - powermetrics may not work"
    fi

    # Start the exporter
    "$BINARY_PATH" -addr ":$EXPORTER_PORT" &
    local pid=$!
    echo "$pid" > "$PID_FILE"
    log_info "Exporter started (PID: $pid)"
}

# Stop the exporter
stop_exporter() {
    if [ -f "$PID_FILE" ]; then
        local pid=$(cat "$PID_FILE")
        if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
            kill "$pid"
            rm -f "$PID_FILE"
            log_info "Exporter stopped"
        else
            log_warn "Exporter process not found"
            rm -f "$PID_FILE"
        fi
    else
        log_warn "No PID file found"
    fi

    # Also try to stop via launchctl
    launchctl unload "$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/${HELPER_LABEL}.plist" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Check if exporter is running
status_exporter() {
    if [ -f "$PID_FILE" ]; then
        local pid=$(cat "$PID_FILE")
        if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
            log_info "Exporter is running (PID: $pid)"
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Also check via launchctl
    if launchctl list | grep -q "$HELPER_LABEL"; then
        log_info "Exporter is running (via launchctl)"
        return 0
    fi

    log_info "Exporter is not running"
    return 1
}

# Open metrics page in browser
open_metrics() {
    open "http://localhost:${EXPORTER_PORT}/metrics"
}

# Show usage
usage() {
    echo "Usage: $0 {start|stop|status|install|uninstall|open}"
    echo ""
    echo "Commands:"
    echo "  start      Start the exporter"
    echo "  stop       Stop the exporter"
    echo "  status     Check exporter status"
    echo "  install    Install launch agent (auto-start)"
    echo "  uninstall  Uninstall launch agent"
    echo "  open       Open metrics page in browser"
}

# Main
main() {
    check_powermetrics

    case "${1:-status}" in
        start)
            start_exporter
            ;;
        stop)
            stop_exporter
            ;;
        status)
            status_exporter
            ;;
        install)
            install_launch_agent
            start_exporter
            ;;
        uninstall)
            stop_exporter
            uninstall_launch_agent
            ;;
        open)
            open_metrics
            ;;
        *)
            usage
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
}

main "$@"

# Proposal: Deploy Wrapper Script to `/usr/local/bin` During Installation

## Summary

As part of the installation process, deploy a bash wrapper script to `/usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh` that provides a convenient CLI interface to the exporter. The script will be owned by `root:wheel` and deployed using sudo privileges requested from the user during installation.

## Motivation

Currently, users must either:
1. Run the exporter binary directly with `sudo ./macos-power-consumption-exporter`
2. Use the DMG-installed launcher application with its menu bar interface

A wrapper script in `/usr/local/bin` would provide a cleaner CLI experience:
- Users could type `macos-power-consumption` from any terminal session
- The script can handle sudo privilege elevation automatically
- Provides a consistent, discoverable command-line interface
- Aligns with Unix conventions for system binaries in `/usr/local/bin`

## Proposed Solution

### 1. Wrapper Script Content

The wrapper script `macos-power-consumption.sh` will be deployed to `/usr/local/bin/` and will:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#
# macOS Power Consumption Exporter - CLI Wrapper
# Provides convenient access to the power consumption exporter
#

set -e

# Configuration
EXPORTER_PORT="${EXPORTER_PORT:-8080}"
APP Bundle path (determined at install time)

# Default to running the exporter if no arguments provided
if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Starting macOS Power Consumption Exporter on port $EXPORTER_PORT..."
    exec sudo /Applications/"MacOS Power Consumption Exporter.app/Contents/MacOS/macos-power-consumption-exporter" -addr ":$EXPORTER_PORT"
fi

# Handle CLI arguments
case "$1" in
    start)
        exec sudo /Applications/"MacOS Power Consumption Exporter.app/Contents/MacOS/macos-power-consumption-exporter" -addr ":$EXPORTER_PORT"
        ;;
    stop)
        pkill -f macos-power-consumption-exporter || echo "Exporter not running"
        ;;
    status)
        if pgrep -f macos-power-consumption-exporter > /dev/null; then
            echo "Exporter is running"
            exit 0
        else
            echo "Exporter is not running"
            exit 1
        fi
        ;;
    metrics)
        open "http://localhost:${EXPORTER_PORT}/metrics"
        ;;
    health)
        open "http://localhost:${EXPORTER_PORT}/health"
        ;;
    restart)
        pkill -f macos-power-consumption-exporter 2>/dev/null || true
        sleep 1
        exec sudo /Applications/"MacOS Power Consumption Exporter.app/Contents/MacOS/macos-power-consumption-exporter" -addr ":$EXPORTER_PORT"
        ;;
    -h|--help|help)
        echo "Usage: macos-power-consumption [command]"
        echo ""
        echo "Commands:"
        echo "  start    Start the exporter (default)"
        echo "  stop     Stop the exporter"
        echo "  status   Check if exporter is running"
        echo "  restart  Restart the exporter"
        echo "  metrics  Open metrics page in browser"
        echo "  health   Open health check page in browser"
        echo ""
        echo "Environment variables:"
        echo "  EXPORTER_PORT    Port to run the exporter on (default: 8080)"
        ;;
    *)
        echo "Unknown command: $1"
        echo "Run 'macos-power-consumption --help' for usage"
        exit 1
        ;;
esac
```

### 2. Deployment During Installation

#### DMG Installer Path

The script will be deployed during the DMG installer's post-install phase. The installation flow will:

1. User drags app to Applications folder
2. User runs the launcher for first time (via Terminal or clicking "Open")
3. The launcher script prompts for sudo password (once)
4. Launcher deploys the wrapper script to `/usr/local/bin/`
5. Launcher sets ownership to `root:wheel` and permissions to `755`
6. Launcher starts the exporter service

#### Command-Line Install Path

For users installing from source:

```bash
# After building
sudo make install
```

The `install` target will:
1. Copy the wrapper script to `/usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh`
2. Set ownership to `root:wheel`
3. Set permissions to `755`

### 3. File Permissions and Ownership

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Path | `/usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh` |
| Owner | `root` |
| Group | `wheel` |
| Mode | `755` (rwxr-xr-x) |

### 4. Installation Prompts

During installation, users will be informed:

```
Installing macOS Power Consumption Exporter CLI wrapper...

This will install a wrapper script to /usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh
Ownership: root:wheel
Permissions: 755

[sudo] password for user:
```

The sudo password is requested only once and cached for the duration of the installation session.

### 5. Upgrade Behavior

When a newer version is installed:

1. **Existing script is replaced** - The wrapper script will be overwritten with the new version
2. **User is notified** - A message will indicate the wrapper script has been updated
3. **No data loss** - The exporter configuration and data remain intact

### 6. Uninstallation Updates

The uninstallation process will be updated to:

1. Remove the wrapper script from `/usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh`
2. Remove the launch agent
3. Remove the application bundle
4. Clean up logs and cache

## Implementation Details

### File Structure Changes

```
installer/
├── app/
│   ├── launcher.sh              # Updated to deploy wrapper script
│   └── wrapper-template.sh      # NEW: Template for wrapper script
├── scripts/
│   ├── install-wrapper.sh       # NEW: Standalone wrapper installation script
│   └── uninstall.sh             # Updated to remove wrapper script
```

### Makefile Changes

```makefile
# New target for wrapper installation
install-wrapper:
	@chmod +x installer/app/wrapper-template.sh
	@sudo install -o root -g wheel -m 755 installer/app/wrapper-template.sh /usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh
	@echo "Wrapper script installed to /usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh"

# Updated uninstall target
uninstall-wrapper:
	@sudo rm -f /usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh
	@echo "Wrapper script removed"

# Combined install
install-full: install-wrapper
	@echo "Full installation complete"
```

### Launcher Script Updates

The `installer/app/launcher.sh` will be updated to:

1. Add a function `install_wrapper_script()` that:
   - Checks if script already exists
   - Prompts for sudo password
   - Installs the script to `/usr/local/bin/`
   - Sets correct ownership and permissions

2. Call `install_wrapper_script()` during `install` command

3. Handle errors gracefully:
   - If sudo fails, warn but continue (wrapper is optional)
   - If file exists, ask whether to overwrite

## Security Considerations

1. **Sudo privilege requirement** - The wrapper script requires sudo to run `powermetrics`, which is unavoidable. We request this once during installation and cache it.

2. **Script integrity** - The wrapper script will be signed along with the DMG to prevent tampering.

3. **Permissions** - Setting `755` ensures only root can modify the script, while everyone can execute it.

4. **Path safety** - Using `/usr/local/bin/` is standard and won't conflict with system binaries.

5. **No arbitrary code execution** - The script only executes the known-good binary in the app bundle.

## User Experience

### First-time Installation (DMG)

```
$ cd "/Applications/MacOS Power Consumption Exporter.app/Contents/MacOS"
$ sudo ./launcher install

This will install:
  - Launch agent for auto-start
  - CLI wrapper script at /usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh

[sudo] password for user:
Installing wrapper script... done
Installing launch agent... done
Starting exporter... done

Success! The exporter is now running.

CLI usage: macos-power-consumption [command]
Web UI: http://localhost:8080/metrics
```

### Source Installation

```
$ make install-wrapper
[sudo] password:
Installing wrapper script... done

$ macos-power-consumption start
Exporter starting on port 8080...
```

## Alternatives Considered

### 1. Deploy without sudo (user-owned script)

**Rejected** because:
- The actual exporter requires sudo anyway to run `powermetrics`
- A user-owned script would still need sudo when executed
- `root:wheel` ownership is the Unix convention for system binaries in `/usr/local/bin/`

### 2. Use a different path (e.g., `~/.local/bin/`)

**Rejected** because:
- Less discoverable for users expecting standard Unix layout
- Each user would need to install separately on multi-user systems
- Doesn't align with the project's "system-level" nature

### 3. Bundle as a LaunchDaemon instead of user-level launch agent

**Rejected** because:
- LaunchDaemons run as root and require more complex setup
- User-level launch agents are sufficient for this use case
- Simpler to install and uninstall

## Open Questions

1. **Should the wrapper script be deployed automatically during app first-run, or as a separate optional step?**

2. **How should we handle systems where `/usr/local/bin/` is not in the default PATH?**

3. **Should we provide an uninstaller option to remove the wrapper script while keeping the app installed?**

4. **Should the wrapper script support custom port via command-line argument (e.g., `macos-power-consumption --port 9090 start`)?**

## Conclusion

This feature provides a convenient CLI interface to the macOS Power Consumption Exporter while maintaining security through proper ownership and permissions. The wrapper script deployment integrates seamlessly into the existing installation process and enhances the overall user experience.

## Status

**Proposed** - Awaiting feedback and approval for implementation.

### 2. Deployment During Installation

#### DMG Installer Path

The script will be deployed during the DMG installer's post-install phase. The installation flow will:

1. User drags app to Applications folder
2. User runs the launcher for first time (via Terminal or clicking "Open")
3. The launcher script prompts for sudo password (once)
4. Launcher deploys the wrapper script to `/usr/local/bin/`
5. Launcher sets ownership to `root:wheel` and permissions to `755`
6. Launcher starts the exporter service

1. Copy the wrapper script to `/usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh`
2. Set ownership to `root:wheel`
3. Set permissions to `755`

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Path | `/usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh` |
| Owner | `root` |
| Group | `wheel` |
| Mode | `755` (rwxr-xr-x) |

```

This will install a wrapper script to /usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh
Ownership: root:wheel
Permissions: 755

[sudo] password for user:
```

The sudo password is requested only once and cached for the duration of the installation session.

### 5. Upgrade Behavior

When a newer version is installed:

1. **Existing script is replaced** - The wrapper script will be overwritten with the new version
2. **User is notified** - A message will indicate the wrapper script has been updated
3. **No data loss** - The exporter configuration and data remain intact

### 6. Uninstallation Updates

1. Remove the wrapper script from `/usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh`
2. Remove the launch agent
3. Remove the application bundle
4. Clean up logs and cache

### File Structure Changes

```
installer/
├── app/
│   ├── launcher.sh              # Updated to deploy wrapper script
│   └── wrapper-template.sh      # NEW: Template for wrapper script
├── scripts/
│   ├── install-wrapper.sh       # NEW: Standalone wrapper installation script
│   └── uninstall.sh             # Updated to remove wrapper script
```

### Makefile Changes

```makefile
# New target for wrapper installation

	@chmod +x installer/app/wrapper-template.sh
	@sudo install -o root -g wheel -m 755 installer/app/wrapper-template.sh /usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh
	@echo "Wrapper script installed to /usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh"

# Updated uninstall target

	@sudo rm -f /usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh
	@echo "Wrapper script removed"

install-full: install-wrapper
	@echo "Full installation complete"
```

### Launcher Script Updates

The `installer/app/launcher.sh` will be updated to:

1. Add a function `install_wrapper_script()` that:
   - Checks if script already exists
   - Prompts for sudo password
   - Installs the script to `/usr/local/bin/`
   - Sets correct ownership and permissions

2. Call `install_wrapper_script()` during `install` command

3. Handle errors gracefully:
   - If sudo fails, warn but continue (wrapper is optional)
   - If file exists, ask whether to overwrite

## Security Considerations

1. **Sudo privilege requirement** - The wrapper script requires sudo to run `powermetrics`, which is unavoidable. We request this once during installation and cache it.

2. **Script integrity** - The wrapper script will be signed along with the DMG to prevent tampering.

3. **Permissions** - Setting `755` ensures only root can modify the script, while everyone can execute it.

4. **Path safety** - Using `/usr/local/bin/` is standard and won't conflict with system binaries.

5. **No arbitrary code execution** - The script only executes the known-good binary in the app bundle.

## User Experience

### First-time Installation (DMG)

```
$ cd "/Applications/MacOS Power Consumption Exporter.app/Contents/MacOS"
$ sudo ./launcher install

This will install:
  - Launch agent for auto-start
  - CLI wrapper script at /usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh

[sudo] password for user:
Installing wrapper script... done
Installing launch agent... done
Starting exporter... done

Success! The exporter is now running.

CLI usage: macos-power-consumption [command]
Web UI: http://localhost:8080/metrics
```

### Source Installation

```
$ make install-wrapper
[sudo] password:
Installing wrapper script... done

$ macos-power-consumption start
Exporter starting on port 8080...
```

## Alternatives Considered

### 1. Deploy without sudo (user-owned script)

**Rejected** because:
- The actual exporter requires sudo anyway to run `powermetrics`
- A user-owned script would still need sudo when executed
- `root:wheel` ownership is the Unix convention for system binaries in `/usr/local/bin/`

### 2. Use a different path (e.g., `~/.local/bin/`)

**Rejected** because:
- Less discoverable for users expecting standard Unix layout
- Each user would need to install separately on multi-user systems
- Doesn't align with the project's "system-level" nature

### 3. Bundle as a LaunchDaemon instead of user-level launch agent

**Rejected** because:
- LaunchDaemons run as root and require more complex setup
- User-level launch agents are sufficient for this use case
- Simpler to install and uninstall

## Open Questions

1. **Should the wrapper script be deployed automatically during app first-run, or as a separate optional step?**

2. **How should we handle systems where `/usr/local/bin/` is not in the default PATH?**

3. **Should we provide an uninstaller option to remove the wrapper script while keeping the app installed?**

4. **Should the wrapper script support custom port via command-line argument (e.g., `macos-power-consumption --port 9090 start`)?**

## Conclusion

This feature provides a convenient CLI interface to the macOS Power Consumption Exporter while maintaining security through proper ownership and permissions. The wrapper script deployment integrates seamlessly into the existing installation process and enhances the overall user experience.

## Analysis: How the Installer Deploys the Wrapper Script

### Installation Flow

The deployment happens in two scenarios:

---

### 1. DMG Installation (Primary Use Case)

**When:** User runs `sudo ./launcher install` from the mounted DMG's app bundle

**Step-by-step process:**

```
1. User navigates to app bundle MacOS directory
   cd "/Applications/MacOS Power Consumption Exporter.app/Contents/MacOS"

2. User runs: sudo ./launcher install

3. launcher.sh prompts for sudo password (once)
   [sudo] password for user:

4. launcher.sh executes install_wrapper_script() function which:
   a. Copies wrapper-template.sh to /usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh
   b. Changes ownership to root:wheel using chown
   c. Changes permissions to 755 using chmod
   
5. launcher.sh proceeds with launch agent installation

6. launcher.sh calls start_exporter() which calls ./launcher start
```

**Key implementation detail:** The wrapper script template would be stored inside the app bundle at `Contents/MacOS/wrapper-template.sh` (or in `Resources/`). The launcher copies from there to `/usr/local/bin/`.

---

### 2. Source Installation (Secondary)

**When:** User runs `make install-wrapper` after building from source

**Step-by-step process:**

```
1. User clones repo and builds
   git clone ... && cd macos-power-consumption-exporter
   make build

2. User runs: sudo make install-wrapper
   (Makefile target runs: sudo install -o root -g wheel -m 755 ...)

3. Makefile target copies wrapper-template.sh to /usr/local/bin/

4. Sets ownership and permissions in one command via install utility
```

**Note:** In this case, the app bundle doesn't exist yet (no DMG built), so the wrapper script would reference the launcher's expected location at `/Applications/...`. The assumption is the user would later install the DMG/app bundle to that location.

---

### Technical Details of Deployment

| Aspect | Details |
|--------|---------|
| **Source file** | `installer/app/wrapper-template.sh` (template, not yet instantiated) |
| **Destination** | `/usr/local/bin/macos-power-consumption.sh` |
| **Ownership** | `root:wheel` (chown root:wheel) |
| **Permissions** | `755` (rwxr-xr-x) - owner can write, others can read/execute |
| **Sudo required** | Yes - only root can change ownership to root:wheel |

### Sudo Password Handling

The installer uses macOS's standard sudo elevation:
- Password is requested once during `sudo ./launcher install`
- sudo caches the credential for ~5 minutes
- All subsequent operations (file copy, chown, launch agent load) use the cached credential

### Error Scenarios

1. **User cancels sudo prompt** → Installation fails at wrapper script step; launch agent not installed either

2. **`/usr/local/bin/` not writable** → Error message; installer suggests running with proper sudo

3. **Wrapper script already exists** → Existing proposal suggests prompting user to overwrite or skip

4. **App bundle moved/deleted** → Wrapper script will fail at runtime when calling launcher; this is a runtime error, not installation error

### Why This Design?

The wrapper script delegates to the launcher rather than directly executing the binary because:
1. **Launcher is already trusted** - It's part of the app bundle
2. **Launcher has proper PID management** - Avoids duplicate processes
3. **Launcher handles launch agent** - Manages auto-start configuration
4. **Single source of truth** - All start/stop logic lives in launcher.sh

#!/bin/bash
#
# macOS Power Consumption Exporter - Application Launcher
# This script is the entry point for the .app bundle
#

set -e

# Configuration
APP_NAME="MacOS Power Consumption Exporter"
BUNDLE_ID="com.combust.macos-power-consumption-exporter"
HELPER_LABEL="com.combust.macos-power-consumption-exporter"
EXPORTER_PORT="${EXPORTER_PORT:-8080}"
LOG_DIR="$HOME/Library/Logs/com.combust.macos-power-consumption-exporter"
PID_FILE="$HOME/.macos-power-consumption-exporter.pid"

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

log_info() {
    echo -e "${GREEN}[INFO]${NC} $1"
}

log_warn() {
    echo -e "${YELLOW}[WARN]${NC} $1"
}

log_error() {
    echo -e "${RED}[ERROR]${NC} $1"
}

# Get the directory where this script is located
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
BINARY_PATH="$SCRIPT_DIR/../MacOS/macos-power-consumption-exporter"

# Create log directory
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"

# Check if powermetrics is available
check_powermetrics() {
    if ! command -v powermetrics &> /dev/null; then
        log_error "powermetrics command not found. This application requires macOS."
        osascript -e 'display dialog "powermetrics not found. This application requires macOS." with title "Error" buttons {"OK"} with icon stop'
        exit 1
    fi
}

# Check if running with sudo privileges
check_sudo() {
    if [ "$EUID" -ne 0 ]; then
        log_warn "Not running with sudo privileges"
        return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# Install launch agent for current user
install_launch_agent() {
    local plist_dir="$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents"
    local plist_path="$plist_dir/${HELPER_LABEL}.plist"

    mkdir -p "$plist_dir"

    # Create launch agent plist
    cat > "$plist_path" << EOF
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>Label</key>
    <string>${HELPER_LABEL}</string>
    <key>ProgramArguments</key>
    <array>
        <string>${BINARY_PATH}</string>
        <string>-addr</string>
        <string>:${EXPORTER_PORT}</string>
    </array>
    <key>RunAtLoad</key>
    <true/>
    <key>KeepAlive</key>
    <true/>
    <key>StandardOutPath</key>
    <string>${LOG_DIR}/exporter.log</string>
    <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
    <string>${LOG_DIR}/exporter.error.log</string>
    <key>ProcessType</key>
    <string>Interactive</string>
</dict>
</plist>
EOF

    log_info "Launch agent installed at $plist_path"
}

# Uninstall launch agent
uninstall_launch_agent() {
    local plist_path="$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/${HELPER_LABEL}.plist"

    if [ -f "$plist_path" ]; then
        launchctl unload "$plist_path" 2>/dev/null || true
        rm -f "$plist_path"
        log_info "Launch agent uninstalled"
    fi
}

# Start the exporter
start_exporter() {
    # Check if already running
    if [ -f "$PID_FILE" ]; then
        local old_pid=$(cat "$PID_FILE")
        if kill -0 "$old_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
            log_info "Exporter is already running (PID: $old_pid)"
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Request sudo if needed
    if ! check_sudo; then
        log_warn "Starting without sudo - powermetrics may not work"
    fi

    # Start the exporter
    "$BINARY_PATH" -addr ":$EXPORTER_PORT" &
    local pid=$!
    echo "$pid" > "$PID_FILE"
    log_info "Exporter started (PID: $pid)"
}

# Stop the exporter
stop_exporter() {
    if [ -f "$PID_FILE" ]; then
        local pid=$(cat "$PID_FILE")
        if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
            kill "$pid"
            rm -f "$PID_FILE"
            log_info "Exporter stopped"
        else
            log_warn "Exporter process not found"
            rm -f "$PID_FILE"
        fi
    else
        log_warn "No PID file found"
    fi

    # Also try to stop via launchctl
    launchctl unload "$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/${HELPER_LABEL}.plist" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Check if exporter is running
status_exporter() {
    if [ -f "$PID_FILE" ]; then
        local pid=$(cat "$PID_FILE")
        if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
            log_info "Exporter is running (PID: $pid)"
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Also check via launchctl
    if launchctl list | grep -q "$HELPER_LABEL"; then
        log_info "Exporter is running (via launchctl)"
        return 0
    fi

    log_info "Exporter is not running"
    return 1
}

# Open metrics page in browser
open_metrics() {
    open "http://localhost:${EXPORTER_PORT}/metrics"
}

# Show usage
usage() {
    echo "Usage: $0 {start|stop|status|install|uninstall|open}"
    echo ""

#
# macOS Power Consumption Exporter - CLI Wrapper
# Provides convenient access to the power consumption exporter
#

set -e

if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Starting macOS Power Consumption Exporter on port $EXPORTER_PORT..."
    exec sudo "$LAUNCHER_PATH" start
fi

# Handle CLI arguments
case "$1" in
    start)
        exec sudo "$LAUNCHER_PATH" start
        ;;
    stop)
        "$LAUNCHER_PATH" stop
        ;;
    status)
        "$LAUNCHER_PATH" status
        ;;
    metrics)
        open "http://localhost:${EXPORTER_PORT}/metrics"
        ;;
    health)
        open "http://localhost:${EXPORTER_PORT}/health"
        ;;
    restart)
        "$LAUNCHER_PATH" stop
        sleep 1
        exec sudo "$LAUNCHER_PATH" start
        ;;

        ;;
